mainTopic: The end of the משנה on helping with wine and bread made in טומאה, and רב הונא's rule that flowing wine can become יין נסך, defended through the earlier and later versions of the law.
overview: The משנה finishes its rules about helping with wine-making. You may not harvest grapes with a נכרי, and you may not tread or harvest with a Jew who makes his wine in טומאה. You may carry barrels to and from the press with that Jew. A baker who works in טומאה follows the same pattern: no kneading or shaping, but carrying the finished bread is allowed. The גמרא then brings רב הונא, who says that once wine starts to flow, a נכרי's touch can make it יין נסך. Two challenges from our משנה are answered by saying it is talking about a plugged, full press where nothing flows. A third challenge, that the wine outside the pit is permitted, cannot be answered that way. So רב הונא says our משנה follows an earlier ruling, while his rule follows the later one. A ברייתא proves this: at first the חכמים allowed treading with a נכרי, but later they forbade it because of רב הונא's concern.

steps.title: No harvesting grapes with a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends its rule about working with a נכרי: you may not harvest grapes with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one may not harvest grapes with him.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a rule from the משנה about working alongside a נכרי in wine-making: harvesting with him is not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The harvested grapes will be brought to the נכרי's winepress, which is טמא. That would make the grapes טמא, and making produce of ארץ ישראל טמא is not allowed. So harvesting is forbidden even though other help in the משנה is allowed.

phrases.english: But one may not harvest grapes with him.
phrases.notes: "Him" is the non-Jew from the earlier part of the משנה, where treading grapes with him was allowed.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Harvesting grapes together with a נכרי is forbidden.

steps.title: A Jew who makes his wine in impurity
steps.stepSummary: You may not press or harvest with a Jew who makes his wine in טומאה. You may carry barrels to and from the winepress with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Jew who makes his wine in ritual impurity: one may not tread or harvest with him. But one may carry barrels with him to the winepress and bring them back with him from the winepress.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a new case: a fellow Jew who makes his wine in טומאה. It says which kinds of help are forbidden and which are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Treading and harvesting are forbidden because they help him do something wrong. Carrying the barrels is allowed because by then the wine is already טמא, so the help adds nothing to the wrongdoing.

keyTerms.meaning: produces his food or wine in a state of ritual impurity
treading on grapes to press them

phrases.english: A Jew who makes his wine in ritual impurity —
one may not tread or harvest with him,
but one may carry barrels with him to the winepress,
and one may bring them with him from the winepress.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the נכרי to a Jew who works in טומאה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not help a Jew in the actual making of wine in טומאה. Carrying barrels to and from the press is allowed.

steps.title: A baker who makes his bread in impurity
steps.stepSummary: With a baker who works in טומאה, you may not knead or shape the dough. You may carry his finished bread to the bread seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: A baker who makes his bread in ritual impurity: one may not knead or shape the dough with him. But one may carry bread with him to the bread seller.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the same pattern for bread. Making it is off limits, but carrying the finished product is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Kneading and shaping are the actual making of the bread, so helping with them helps the wrongdoing. Once the bread is finished it is already טמא, so carrying it to the seller is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: a bread seller or bread shop

steps.whatToRemember: The rule in both cases: do not help with the making in טומאה, but you may help with carrying the finished product.

phrases.english: A baker who makes his bread in ritual impurity —
one may not knead or shape the dough with him,
but one may carry bread with him to the bread seller.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same pattern as step 2 to bread.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not help with kneading or shaping bread made in טומאה. Carrying the finished bread is allowed.

steps.title: Wine counts once it starts to flow
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says that as soon as the juice starts to flow in the press, it counts as wine that can become יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא says: once wine starts to flow, it can become libation wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב הונא's rule about when grape juice counts as wine for the laws of יין נסך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says we do not wait until the juice reaches the collecting pit. Once it starts flowing, it counts as wine, so a נכרי's touch can make it יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: the discussion that explains the משנה
wine poured for עבודה זרה, which is forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the point at which a נכרי's touch can forbid the wine. The rest of this section tests it against the משנה.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna says:
Wine, once it has started to flow,
phrases.notes: He means the juice starting to run inside the winepress.

phrases.english: can become libation wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: יַיִן, כֵּיוָן שֶׁהִתְחִיל לְהִמָּשֵׁךְ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Juice that has started to flow counts as wine, and a נכרי's touch can make it יין נסך.

steps.title: Challenge from buying a trodden press
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows buying a trodden winepress from a נכרי even though he touched the grapes. Shouldn't the flowing juice already be forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: one may buy a trodden winepress from a non-Jew, even though he took grapes in his hand and put them on the pile!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא with a משנה. It allows the wine even though the נכרי touched the grapes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a trodden press the juice is normally already flowing. According to רב הונא, the נכרי's touch should make it יין נסך. Yet the משנה allows it, which looks like a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: trodden or pressed with the feet
here: the pile of grapes waiting to be pressed

steps.confusionAlert: Here תפוח does not mean an apple. It means a heap of grapes.

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: לוֹקְחִים גַּת בְּעוּטָה מִן הַנׇּכְרִי,
phrases.english: We learned: one may buy a trodden winepress from a non-Jew,
even though he took grapes in his hand
and put them on the pile!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: לוֹקְחִים גַּת בְּעוּטָה מִן הַנׇּכְרִי
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that flowing juice can become יין נסך.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a trodden press the juice is already flowing, yet the משנה allows the wine after a נכרי touched it.

steps.title: The press was plugged and full
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the משנה is talking about a press that is plugged and full, so the juice is not flowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: it is a winepress that is plugged and full.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends his rule by narrowing the case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the press's opening is plugged and the press is full, the juice cannot run anywhere. Since nothing is flowing, it is not yet wine by רב הונא's rule, and the נכרי's touch does no harm.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is a winepress that is plugged and full.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: בְּגַת פְּקוּקָה וּמְלֵאָה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be about an ordinary press where juice flows.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a plugged, full press with no flow, so it fits רב הונא.

steps.title: Challenge: not forbidden until it reaches the pit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says wine does not become יין נסך until it goes down into the pit. That seems to mean flowing alone is not enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: and it does not become libation wine until it goes down into the pit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second line from the משנה that seems to go against רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets the point at reaching the pit, not at the start of flowing. That suggests flowing juice still in the press cannot become יין נסך, which goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: the collecting pit below the press

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, וְאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה יֵין נֶסֶךְ
phrases.english: Come and hear: and it does not become libation wine
until it goes down into the pit!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, וְאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה יֵין נֶסֶךְ עַד שֶׁיֵּרֵד לַבּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב הונא from the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that flowing juice can become יין נסך.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names reaching the pit as the point, which suggests flowing juice before that is not yet forbidden.

steps.title: Again, a plugged and full press
steps.stepSummary: The same answer works here: the משנה is about a plugged, full press where nothing flows.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, it is a winepress that is plugged and full.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer to the second challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a plugged press the juice does not flow at all. So the משנה gives the pit as the point only for that case. In an open press, רב הונא's rule still applies once the juice flows.
steps.whatToRemember: The plugged-and-full-press answer handles the first two challenges to רב הונא. The next step brings a line from the משנה that this answer cannot handle.

phrases.english: Here too, it is a winepress that is plugged and full.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא), reusing the earlier answer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to say all juice in the press is allowed until it reaches the pit.
steps.terutzMaskana: That is only in a plugged, full press where nothing flows.

steps.title: The משנה says the rest of the wine is permitted
steps.stepSummary: A third challenge to רב הונא: the משנה says only what reached the pit is forbidden, and the rest, which is still flowing, is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: once the wine went down into the pit, what is in the pit is forbidden and the rest is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה again to challenge רב הונא. This time the wording seems to openly permit the wine that is still flowing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the גמרא only inferred from the משנה that flowing alone is not enough. Now the משנה says it outright: the wine outside the pit is permitted. That remaining wine is clearly flowing, so the plugged-press answer from steps 6 and 8 cannot work here.

keyTerms.meaning: The pit or collection vat under the winepress, where the juice gathers

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Once it went down into the pit,
what is in the pit is forbidden,
and the rest is permitted.
phrases.notes: 'The rest' means the juice still flowing in the press that has not reached the pit yet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, stronger challenge from the משנה, one that the plugged-press answer cannot handle.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that flowing juice already counts as wine for יין נסך.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה openly permits the wine outside the pit, even though it is flowing. That directly contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: Earlier version versus later version
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the משנה follows the earlier ruling, while his own rule follows the later ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: It is not difficult. Here the משנה follows the first version of the law; there, my rule follows the later version.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the challenge by saying the משנה and his rule come from two different stages of the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא does not reread the משנה's case this time. He says our משנה reflects what the חכמים held at first. His own rule matches what they held later, after they changed their position.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no real contradiction
The first, earlier version of the law
The later, revised version of the law

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'מִשְׁנָה רִאשׁוֹנָה' does not mean 'the first משנה on the page.' It means the earlier stage of the law, before the חכמים changed their minds.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
It is not difficult:
here, it follows the first version of the law;
phrases.notes: 'Here' is our משנה, which permits the flowing wine.

phrases.english: there, it follows the later version.
phrases.notes: 'There' is רב הונא's own rule from step 4.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Two stages of the law: an earlier ruling and a later revised ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to show that flowing wine is permitted, which would disprove רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה reflects the earlier law. The later law, which is the one in force, matches רב הונא.

steps.title: The earlier ruling: treading with a נכרי was allowed
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that at first the חכמים allowed treading grapes together with a נכרי, without worrying about רב הונא's concern.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: At first they said (memory sign: B-D-D): One may not harvest grapes with a נכרי for the press, because it is forbidden to cause טומאה to ordinary produce in ארץ ישראל. One may not tread grapes with a Jew who makes his produce in טומאה, because it is forbidden to help sinners. But one may tread with a נכרי in the press. We are not worried about רב הונא's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove there really was an earlier stage of the law. This is the first half, describing the original rulings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two activities were forbidden at first because of טומאה concerns, but treading together with a נכרי was allowed. That means the חכמים were not yet worried that the נכרי's touch makes the flowing juice forbidden. That fits our משנה, which permits flowing wine.

keyTerms.meaning: To help people who are doing a sin
We are not worried about it

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
At first they would say: "B-D-D":
phrases.notes: These letters are a memory sign: ב for בוצרין (harvesting), ד for דורכין (treading), ד for דורכין again.

phrases.english: One may not harvest grapes with a non-Jew for the winepress,
because it is forbidden to cause impurity
to ordinary produce in the Land of Israel,
and one may not tread grapes with a Jew
who makes his produce in impurity,
because it is forbidden to help those who sin,
but one may tread with the non-Jew in the winepress,
and we are not worried about Rav Huna's rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings proof for the 'earlier version' half of רב הונא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: That there was an earlier stage of the law in which flowing wine touched by a נכרי was not treated as forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording that at first, treading with a נכרי was permitted.

steps.title: The later ruling: treading with a נכרי was forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: later the חכמים forbade treading with a נכרי, because of רב הונא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they changed and said (memory sign: D-B-B): One may not tread with a נכרי in the winepress, because of רב הונא's rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by showing that the חכמים later changed the law and forbade treading with a נכרי. This completes the proof for רב הונא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason given for the change is רב הונא's concern. While treading, the נכרי touches the flowing juice, which already counts as wine and becomes forbidden. So the later law supports רב הונא, and our משנה reflects the older law.

keyTerms.meaning: And they changed their minds and said

steps.whatToRemember: Our משנה, which permits wine until it reaches the pit, follows the earlier law. The חכמים later changed the law and forbade treading with a נכרי, because flowing juice already counts as wine. That is רב הונא's rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the later practice is stricter than our משנה: the final law follows רב הונא.

phrases.english: And they changed and said: "D-B-B":
phrases.notes: Another memory sign. Some versions read the letters as ד-ב-ד, with ד for treading and ב for harvesting.

phrases.english: One may not tread grapes with the non-Jew in the winepress,
because of Rav Huna's rule.
phrases.notes: The נכרי touches the flowing juice while treading, and flowing juice already counts as wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא's proof by showing the later, revised law.
steps.raayaObject: That the later law matches רב הונא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second half of the ברייתא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא's rule follows the later, final law. The משנה that permits flowing wine reflects the earlier law that was later changed.
